fix(viewer): allow externally hosted images in shared packages (exelearning#2684)

Closes exelearning/exelearning#2684

Thanks @luismiglesias for the detailed report, the reproduction steps made this a one-line hunt.

## Problem

The runtime Service Worker (`public/runtime/sw.js`) serves every file of the
package with a Content-Security-Policy that only allowed package-local,
`data:` and `blob:` resources:

```
img-src 'self' data: blob:; media-src 'self' data: blob:
```

An image inserted in the editor with an external URL (the issue's
`https://cdn.pixabay.com/...`) is therefore blocked by the browser the moment
the package is rendered in the viewer — hence the blank space. The editor is
unaffected because it never goes through this worker.

Same root cause for every other externally hosted asset: remote video/audio,
web fonts, external stylesheets and embeds (YouTube and friends) were blocked
too, so the fix is applied to those directives as well rather than to `img-src`
alone.

## Solution

Allow `https:` for passive remote content (`img-src`, `media-src`, `font-src`,
`style-src`, `frame-src`) and add an explicit `script-src` that keeps code
package-local. `connect-src` is deliberately left to fall back to
`default-src 'self'`, so a package still cannot run external code or phone
home.

## Tests

New `src/sw/runtime-sw.test.ts` drives `sw.js` with a stand-in
`ServiceWorkerGlobalScope` (it is a plain script, not bundled by Vite),
registers a session and asserts the served CSP: `img-src`/`media-src` allow
`https:`, `script-src` does not.

- Red before the fix: `expected 'img-src 'self' data: blob:' to contain 'https:'`
- Green after it.

Full validation: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (9 files, 52 tests), `npm run build`,
`make -n …`, `git diff --check` — all clean. `biome ci` reports one pre-existing
warning in `src/style.css`, untouched here.

## Screenshots

A page served with the **old** CSP header and the exact image URL from the issue,
then with the **new** one:

![csp-before.jpg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c6ac3c3-cacb-4ec0-a16e-6e70dfa77cc9)

![csp-after.jpg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5693d0bf-b532-4b11-8b08-d9e799b827e8)

(The end-to-end path — real Drive file plus public share link — needs a
published build, so the capture isolates the header that changed.)

fix(test): stabilize month-boundary dates and session request checks

Woodpecker #114 exposed two E2E assumptions: selecting a date in an adjacent month without navigating the calendar, and requiring exactly one Session request when Apollo can reuse cached metadata.

The date helper now navigates months before selecting. A regression selects day 15 in both adjacent months and clears the date. The navigation test waits for initial metadata and computed content, then enforces at most one refresh. A component test directly verifies that FutureDayPage queries only projects and day data and uses its parent's session token; deliberately adding its own Session query makes this test fail. Both navigation scenarios now run in PR checks. No application behavior, timeouts, or retries changed.

Validation after the final edits: task validate, task test (337 frontend tests plus Go race/shuffle tests), task gen:check; all 195 service-mode E2E tests and all 16 service-mode PR tests. Review found no remaining issues. Disposable test containers and networks were removed.

fix(acp): resolve OpenCode part ids before classification

## Problem

OpenCode 1.x can emit `agent_thought_chunk` updates with a `prt_...` part ID in `messageId`. The compaction stream used that value as the native message ID for `/session/:id/message/:messageID`, which requires `msg_...`; OpenCode returned HTTP 400 and the ACP stream terminated.

## Proposed change

Normalize malformed OpenCode part identities at the ACP ingress. Resolve each `prt_...` through the session message list, validate that it belongs to the assistant message for the active session, and rewrite the update to the parent `msg_...` before SDK delivery. Classification and compaction lifecycle events use the same canonical identity. The mapping cache is cleared on connection cleanup and session close/delete.

## Scope and non-goals

- Covers OpenCode 1.x ACP message and thought chunks, including replay.
- Keeps native OpenCode history unchanged.
- No persisted data, enum, UI, or migration changes.
- Does not change Claude Code, Codex, or Codex bridge paths.

## Acceptance criteria and validation

- `prt_...` chunks never reach the SDK or message-detail endpoint as message IDs.
- Summary chunks remain hidden while lifecycle events use the parent `msg_...`.
- Ordinary reasoning chunks are delivered with the canonical `msg_...`.
- Focused Vitest: 11 tests passed.
- ESLint passed for the changed module and test.
- Prettier passed.

The focused checks ran after the final material edit. Full `npm test` is delegated to CI as requested; local worktree dependency installation could not resolve the npm registry in this environment.

## Review focus

- ACP ingress normalization and cache invalidation across replay and session directory changes.
- Fail-closed validation of the session message list before rewriting an identity.

fix(build): only migrate from preview builds when previews are opted in

## What & why
Vercel builds every PR branch as a preview, and **Preview shares Production's `DATABASE_URL`**. Every build runs `apps/api/scripts/deploy-migrate.mjs`, so a PR's preview build applies that PR's migrations to the **live** database before anyone reviews or merges it.

This already happened once. PR #129's preview applied `0013_doctor_reports` to production. Production `/api/health?db=1` now shows 13 known migrations plus 1 unknown, and #129's own preview, on the same database, shows 14/14.

The fix:
- Vercel **preview** builds skip migrations unless `MIGRATE_ON_PREVIEW=1` is set.
- **Production**, **Docker**, and **local** builds behave exactly as before.
- The decision lives in `apps/api/scripts/deploy-migrate-policy.mjs`, a pure function with unit tests.

**Follow-up (owner, in Vercel):** a Neon `preview` branch now exists. The next step is to give Preview its own `DATABASE_URL` pointing at that branch, then set `MIGRATE_ON_PREVIEW=1` for Preview, so previews migrate their own copy.

## How it was tested
- `tests/deploy-migrate-policy.test.mjs` passes 3/3, including the regression case: preview plus a remote URL means skip, unless the value is exactly `MIGRATE_ON_PREVIEW=1`.
- **Real script, preview:** `VERCEL_ENV=preview DATABASE_URL=<remote>` logs "Vercel preview build … — skipping migrations" and exits 0, with no connection attempt.
- **Real script, production:** `VERCEL_ENV=production` still goes to the migration step.
- `pnpm lint` and the API typecheck pass.
- **This PR's own Vercel preview** should log the skip line in its build output.

## Risk & rollback
- **Risk:** low. The only behaviour change is for Vercel preview builds. A preview of a PR that adds a migration will lack the new schema until previews have their own database and opt in. That's the intended trade-off.
- **Rollback:** revert the commit.

## Docs / OpenAPI / .env.example updated?
The new `MIGRATE_ON_PREVIEW` setting is documented in the policy module header. It's Vercel-only, so it isn't added to `.env.example`.

## Migration?

fix: target llama.cpp stats to displayed model

llama.cpp router servers reject bare `/metrics` and `/slots` requests with HTTP 400, leaving speed, token and slot data empty. Resolve health and models first, then request both optional endpoints with the safely encoded ID of the model already displayed.

Validation: the existing llama.cpp spec passes all 26 tests; six actual-source HTTP fixture cases pass without request rewriting, including router and reserved-character IDs. The same router fixture changes from HTTP 400/null stats to HTTP 200/populated stats. Optional-endpoint and empty-roster behavior stays unchanged. Changed-file formatting and lint checks pass.

Refs #7141

BUGFIX: Move dialogs in front of secondary inspectors

Secondary inspectors are at z-index 60, but dialogs at 55, which led to dialogs being hidden from the user. With this change they are now in front of any inspector with a z-index of 65.

Resolves: #3849
